Key points
• To determine the nutritional composition of major types of nuts and seeds grown for human consumption.
• To update the health beneﬁts of nuts and seeds according to the latest research.
• To learn some curiosities about nuts and seeds.
In botanical terms, the word “nut” is used to describe a wide range of seeds, mostly from trees; however, there are some exceptions.
Peanuts are the seeds of a legume and other nuts grow inside of leathery fruits. Nuts include among others the almond, cashew,
chestnut, Brazil nut, hazelnut, macadamia, peanut, pecan, pine nut, pistachio and walnut. Nuts and seeds come from a diverse range
of different plants (vegetables, ﬂowers, or crops grown for a variety of uses), so their nutritional composition is quite varied. Seeds,
such as pumpkin seeds, sesame and sunﬂower, are sources of protein, unsaturated fatty acids, various micronutrients, and ﬁber
(non-starch polysaccharides (NSP)). Nuts and seeds have a wide range of uses. In the typical Western diet or Mediterranean diet
they tend to be used either as snack items or added as minor ingredient to savory and sweet dishes, but they have wider applications
